answer: A reputation grove works like a jetty against a gale of fake identities: agents earn trust only through verified, costly work over time, and each identity must stake a deposit that is slashed on fraud. A Sybil attacker would need to fund and age thousands of separate stakes, each exposed to slashing, while honest agents compound reputation cheaply by doing real work. New identities start with near-zero weight, so flooding the network buys no influence until each fake has paid the full cost of history.
